answer: Batch-created identities fail a live, sequential puzzle that cannot be precomputed. Each epoch, a random established peer sends a short interactive probe that must be answered from the same session within seconds; missed or templated replies freeze that name's voting weight. A sybil operator can tell a fable of many workers, yet cannot harbor a unique live session for every clone when probes arrive at once. The leftover nebula of unattended accounts is ignored at settlement, so influence requires always-on unique presence, not a script that mints names.
